meta.title: CGA GPU Annealer on a Hard CO2RR Catalyst-Portfolio QUBO
meta.oneLiner: GPU-accelerated simulated annealing benchmark on a hard CO2RR catalyst portfolio QUBO instance.

problem.summary: Select a diverse, high-value batch of CO2 electroreduction (CO2RR -> CO) catalyst candidates from a predicted pool under a fixed validation budget. The selection trades predicted catalytic utility against pairwise chemical redundancy and enforces an exactly-K cardinality constraint.
problem.objective: Minimize the QUBO objective combining singleton utility, pairwise redundancy penalty, and a cardinality penalty that enforces exactly K selected sites.

scale.description: 100 candidate catalyst sites; select K=25 with beta=5 pairwise coupling (hard synthetic regime).

problem.currentApproach: Greedy marginal selection iteratively picks the candidate with highest utility net of already-selected redundancy.
constraints: No additional explicit constraints; redundancy is encoded as a pairwise QUBO penalty.
problem.formulation: Binary QUBO with variables y_j in {0,1}; objective E(y) = -sum_j V_j y_j + beta sum_{i<j} S_{ij} y_i y_j + lambda_K (sum_j y_j - K)^2.
problem.objectiveLatex: E(y) = -\sum_{j} V_j y_j + \beta \sum_{i<j} S_{ij}^{\text{chem}} y_i y_j + \lambda_K \left(\sum_j y_j - K\right)^2

primary.name: QUBO objective value
primary.baselineSource: Greedy marginal solver on hard_N100K25B5 cell

secondary.name: Gap to certified optimum
secondary.baselineSource: Greedy gap to Gurobi MIQP optimum (0.5074) on hard_N100K25B5

chosen.name: CGA GPU annealer
chosen.rationale: A third-party GPU-accelerated simulated annealing service used as an independent annealing reference to compare against classical greedy, SA, and D-Wave Hybrid on the identical QUBO instance.

alternatives.name: Greedy marginal selection
alternatives.whyNot: Faster and feasible, but yields a higher objective (5.3467) than CGA (4.7700) in this hard regime.

alternatives.name: D-Wave Hybrid
alternatives.whyNot: Achieves the certified optimum vicinity (0.5074) but requires D-Wave Leap access; CGA was evaluated as an additional independent annealing reference.

alternatives.name: Gurobi MIQP
alternatives.whyNot: Certified optimum (0.5074) used as the bound/reference; not a heuristic solver being compared.

optimality.boundSource: Gurobi MIQP certified optimum on hard_N100K25B5
optimality.interpretation: CGA returns a feasible solution but leaves a large gap to the certified optimum in this strongly coupled, high-selection-fraction regime.

performance.note: Wall time includes Socket.IO connection, server queueing, GPU anneal, and sample decode. Server-reported anneal time was 34.20 s.

qualitative: Demonstrates that GPU annealing is feasible on the CO2RR chemical QUBO via a standard Socket.IO interface.
Provides an independent annealing reference point alongside D-Wave Hybrid and Fujitsu DA.
value.caveat: The hard regime is a synthetic stress test (K/N=0.25, beta=5), not the realistic closed-loop validation budget (K/N ~ 0.025).

figures.heading: Solver gap to best-known
figures.caption: Bar chart of solver gap to best-known energy on identical locked QUBO instances (K=10, beta=1), including CGA GPU annealer.
figures.alt: Bar chart showing solver gaps across N=50,100,200,272 for greedy, SA, SQA, Fujitsu DA, HiGHS, D-Wave Hybrid, D-Wave QPU, Gurobi, and CGA GPU.

reproduce.dataNote: Candidate pool derived from Catalysis-Hub exact-facet CO*/H* pairs (402 candidates). The hard_N100K25B5 cell is a synthetic subsample with K=25, beta=5, lambda_K=5.

notes.whatWorked: The Socket.IO submission and decode pipeline successfully returned feasible selections on all tested locked and hard cells.
notes.whatDidnt: CGA did not close the gap to Gurobi or D-Wave Hybrid in the hard regime; its objective was comparable to or worse than greedy except on hard_N100K25B5 where it modestly beat greedy.
gotchas: The CGA server renames pyQUBO variables y[j] to c[j]; the client remaps both conventions back to candidate indices.
Server queueing and network overhead add several seconds beyond the anneal budget.
A pyQUBO model is required for automatic constraint violation counting; otherwise a manual spacing/cardinality check is used.
notes.nextTime: Run multiple seeds/repeats per cell, sweep anneal budgets (30/60/120 s), and compare CGA against Fujitsu DA and D-Wave Hybrid under identical time limits.
